title: Small shoulder and upper-spine exploration
summary: A project-authored feasibility movement for comparing the surface, shoulder girdle, spine, and named muscle paths on one shared rig.

instruction.exploration: Notice the relation between the shoulder blades and upper spine while the movement stays small enough to remain easy.

attention.cue: Notice whether one shoulder begins before the other.
Let the return be as gradual as the outward path.

range.smaller_reference: Use a smaller path or imagine the movement if the visible range is not comfortable.

variations.note: Reduce both shoulder and spine movement together.
Rest the forearms on a stable surface.

cautions: Do not continue if the movement increases pain, dizziness, numbness, or tingling.
Use stable support if sitting balance is uncertain.
safety.notes: Educational visualization only; it is not diagnosis, treatment, or individualized movement instruction.

source.tradition_basis: Project-authored description informed by general Feldenkrais principles of attention, optional range, and an unhurried return; no lesson text or recording was copied.
source.rights_basis: provisional: project-authored movement description and project-authored feasibility motion on ledgered local assets
